title: Meta review: the 14 uncovered as_is finding records - evidence re-derived from the bytes each one cites, severities assessed, dispositions checked against the normative vocabulary
lifecycle_status_note: 'draft' rather than 'reviewed' or 'approved': this record is the output of an automated review pass and no human reviewer has confirmed it. The automated_review_status block below refers to corpus automation only and is not a statement about engineering validity.

revision_history.author: quality_engineer
revision_history.description: First issue. Meta review of the finding records: for each record named in reviewed_ids, the claim was re-derived from the bytes it cites rather than read from the record, the severity was assessed, the disposition was checked against the normative vocabulary, and the record's own currency proof was verified to exist and to agree with the corpus. No finding record was modified by this pass.

reviewer_identity.note: Automated review performed in a single AI coding-agent session (opencode). The model identifier is the identifier exposed to this session's runtime. No platform-issued session id was available, so session_id is a locally chosen label for this run and is not a platform-issued identifier. Per master-prompt clause 2.9 this is an automated review: it is NOT organisational independence, NOT human confirmation, and NOT a qualified-checker result. No human reviewer, independent party, or separate agent session participated.

scope: SCOPE: the finding records of the as_is profile only, and specifically the 14 that no review record covered when this pass began. They were identified by an INDEPENDENT recomputation of the automated_review_coverage dimension, written from scratch and not importing corpus.py; the same computation put the dimension at 190/285 with exactly 35 uncovered finding records, 14 of them in this profile and 21 in synthetic_reference. PROFILE IS EXPLICIT AND DELIBERATE: review.schema.json constrains reviewed_ids[].artifact_id to a three-segment id and reviewed_ids has additionalProperties false, so there is no profile field. A profile-scoped review that names both profiles' copies of one finding id would claim coverage of content it did not read; that is the defect recorded as FB2-REV-FND-000198 and FB2-REV-000046, so this record covers the as_is copies only and the synthetic_reference copies are covered by FB2-REV-000023. Each record was read in full and its asserted condition re-derived from the corpus bytes it cites. This record does not review itself, and it does not review any finding record it does not name.

findings.description: The link census that this finding and its two siblings rely on is summed across the profile boundary, so the evidence in an as_is-scoped finding record overstates what the as_is profile contains by a factor of three. FB2-REV-FND-000001 is scoped 'profile': 'as_is' and states, in its resolution and again in its reverification block, that 'FB2-SAF-FSR-000001 in profile as_is is the target of 4 verifies link(s)' and enumerates them: FB2-LNK-SAF-000021, FB2-LNK-SAF-000026, FB2-LNK-SAF-000042, FB2-LNK-SAF-000049. Recomputed from the nine live link registries with the documented precedence order, FB2-SAF-FSR-000001 is the target of exactly ONE verifies link in as_is - FB2-LNK-SAF-000021, from FB2-VER-TMS-000003. The other three named ids are synthetic_reference verifies links; three of the four exist only in the synthetic_reference registry and FB2-LNK-SAF-000026 is a synthetic_reference record that is not a verifies link to FB2-SAF-FSR-000001 in as_is at all. The same arithmetic error appears in FB2-REV-FND-000003 and FB2-REV-FND-000005, where each claims 4 and each actually has 1; and in the synthetic_reference siblings FB2-REV-FND-000002, -000004 and -000006, which claim 4 and each actually have 3. The figure 4 is the SUM of the two profiles (1 + 3). SCOPE OF THE HARM IS EXPLICIT AND SMALL, and is stated so this is not read as a wrong verdict: the condition each record asserts is 'this requirement has no verifies/validates link', and each profile has at least one such link, so condition_still_holds=false is CORRECT in all six records and the 'resolved' disposition and the audit_class STALE verdict both stand. What is wrong is the supporting evidence - the count and the enumerated link ids - which is the exact field a reader opens to check the claim, and it is wrong by a factor of three in the as_is records. Not corrected here: these records were not modified by this pass. The same profile-blind summation is the defect class recorded as FB2-REV-FND-000046 for review records, so this is that class recurring in the evidence of the finding family itself.
findings.evidence: Recomputed from the link registries, not read from the record. In docs/artifacts/traceability/link-registry/as_is/, FB2-SAF-FSR-000001 is the target of exactly one verifies link, FB2-LNK-SAF-000021, sourced by FB2-VER-TMS-000003; FB2-VER-TMS-000008 and FB2-VER-TMS-000011, both named as sources in the record, have no verifies link to FB2-SAF-FSR-000001 in as_is. In the synthetic_reference registries the same requirement has three: FB2-LNK-SAF-000026, FB2-LNK-SAF-000042, FB2-LNK-SAF-000049. Per-requirement counts measured: as_is FB2-SAF-FSR-000001=1, 000002=1, 000003=1, 000004=0 (no such record in as_is); synthetic_reference 000001=3, 000002=3, 000003=3, 000004=3. Recorded claim in all six records: 4. Corroborating that the mechanism itself is real and not in dispute: docs/artifacts/tools/corpus.py line 4993 reads verified = {l["target_id"] for l in links if l.get("relation_type") in ("verifies", "validates") and l.get("target_id")}, so the inversion these six records describe was genuinely fixed.

findings.description: This record's proof-of-currency block contradicts both the source it claims to have re-read and the record's own evidence field. The reverification block of FB2-REV-FND-000036 states: 'FreeRTOS.h:587-592 still defines the three queue-registry functions as empty function-like macros and configQUEUE_REGISTRY_SIZE is still defined nowhere, so the shipped configuration is still exposed: the condition holds.' Two separate problems, both measured. First, configQUEUE_REGISTRY_SIZE IS defined: src/os/freertos/freertos/include/FreeRTOSConfig.h line 78 reads '#define configQUEUE_REGISTRY_SIZE                  ( 0 )'. The record's own evidence field says exactly that, in the same file: 'The shipped FreeRTOSConfig.h:78 sets configQUEUE_REGISTRY_SIZE to 0, so all three are defined.' So the record contradicts itself between two fields of the same revision, and the currency block is the wrong one - which is the field a later reader trusts for whether an OPEN finding still stands. Second, the cited range does not contain the text the record quotes from it: '#ifndef configQUEUE_REGISTRY_SIZE', '#define configQUEUE_REGISTRY_SIZE    0U' and '#endif' are at FreeRTOS.h lines 584, 585 and 586, and the record quotes all three verbatim as part of a block it locates at 587-592; line 587 is blank. THE VERDICT STANDS AND IS NOT DISTURBED BY EITHER ERROR. The asserted condition is that the three queue-registry functions are compiled away, and they are: whether the interval comes from FreeRTOSConfig.h or from FreeRTOS.h's own '#ifndef / #define 0U / #endif' fallback, configQUEUE_REGISTRY_SIZE is 0, the '#if ( configQUEUE_REGISTRY_SIZE < 1 )' at FreeRTOS.h:588 fires, and the three empty function-like macros at :589, :590 and :591 are defined. condition_still_holds=true, audit_class OPEN and the 'accepted' disposition are all correct, and the record's reasoning is otherwise careful - it is recorded as accepted because it names the owner and the three concrete changes that would close it. The defect is confined to the provenance layer: a negative claim about the source that is false, and a line range that omits the lines it quotes. Neither is caught by any tool, because finding.schema.json has no code_location or evidence_files slot: all 42 finding records in this corpus carry neither, so this whole class of citation error is invisible to provenance verification. That is why the correction was made by reading the source rather than by running a check.
findings.evidence: Read from the working tree, not from the record. src/os/freertos/freertos/include/FreeRTOSConfig.h:78 -> '#define configQUEUE_REGISTRY_SIZE                  ( 0 )'. src/os/freertos/freertos/include/FreeRTOS.h:584 '#ifndef configQUEUE_REGISTRY_SIZE', :585 '    #define configQUEUE_REGISTRY_SIZE    0U', :586 '#endif', :587 blank, :588 '#if ( configQUEUE_REGISTRY_SIZE < 1 )', :589-591 the three empty function-like macros, :592 '#endif'. src/os/freertos/freertos/include/queue.h:1564/1579/1594 are the three '#if ( configQUEUE_REGISTRY_SIZE > 0 )' guards whose declarations CMock parses - so the record's mechanism and its queue.h line references are correct, and only the FreeRTOS.h range and the configQUEUE_REGISTRY_SIZE negative claim are wrong. No machine check covers either: corpus.py's provenance pass reports 'code location parts: 82' and 'source anchors: 130', all on non-finding records; the finding family carries 0 source_anchors and 0 evidence_files.

dispositions.action: Accepted as a real evidence defect in six records, three of them in this profile (FB2-REV-FND-000001, -000003, -000005) and three in the sibling record FB2-REV-000023 (FB2-REV-FND-000002, -000004, -000006). The disposition and audit_class of all six are CORRECT and are not disturbed: the condition each one asserts is false in its own profile, because each profile has at least one inbound verifies link. The count and the enumerated link ids in the evidence of all six are wrong for the profile the record claims. NOT CORRECTED HERE: no finding record was modified by this pass. Referred to the finding-record owner to restate the census per profile, which is a one-line edit to six evidence fields and changes no verdict.

Accepted as a real provenance defect in one record. FB2-REV-FND-000036's condition_still_holds, its audit_class OPEN, its 'accepted' disposition, its owner_role and its named closing actions are all correct and are not disturbed; only its reverification sentence about configQUEUE_REGISTRY_SIZE and its FreeRTOS.h line range are wrong. NOT CORRECTED HERE: the record was not modified. Referred to the record owner to correct the negative claim to 'still defined as 0 in FreeRTOSConfig.h:78' and the range to 584-592. Also referred to the schema owner: finding.schema.json has no machine-checked provenance slot, so this class of citation error is undetectable by corpus.py across all 42 finding records.

CANDIDATE WITHDRAWN ON A SECOND READ. Raised as a candidate in this pass and then withdrawn: 'FB2-REV-FND-000022 carries lifecycle_status "reviewed" while its own resolution says no human approved it, so the record self-certifies.' NOT A DEFECT. FB2-REV-FND-000022 carries an explicit lifecycle_status_note that defines the word before a reader can misread it: "'reviewed': the remediation described below was performed and the resulting files were read back and checked. 'reviewed' here means the edits were verified to remove the claimed defects and to leave the document under tool control. It does NOT mean a human approved this finding or the document: human_approval_status remains 'pending' for every artifact." Checked and confirmed: human_approval_status is 'pending', production_authorized false, product_verification_credit false. The same bounded note is present on all 8 findings at lifecycle_status 'reviewed' and on the 1 at 'baselined'. Withdrawn as a check that passed, not as a finding.

CANDIDATE WITHDRAWN ON A SECOND READ. Raised as a candidate and then withdrawn: 'FB2-REV-FND-000038's resolution says the RELAX block adds SEVEN diagnostics while its reverification lists NINE, an unreconciled arithmetic contradiction inside a high-severity record.' NOT A DEFECT - the two statements are scoped differently and both are correct. Read docs/artifacts/.work/verification-env/sil/run.sh: its own header comment at line 8 says RELAX_CLANG_DIAGNOSTICS=1 'additionally silence[s] seven diagnostics', and seven -Wno- entries follow in the env-gated block at lines 659, 660, 669, 675, 679, 685 and 698. Two more, -Wno-strict-prototypes and -Wno-deprecated-non-prototype, are unconditional at lines 610-611 and are described as such in the adjacent comment. Seven gated plus two unconditional is nine, which is exactly the reverification's list. No contradiction. Withdrawn as a check that passed. NOTE: run.sh is under .work/, so this verification is against a working-tree file and is not reproducible from a clean checkout - which is the subject of FB2-REV-FND-000201, not of this withdrawn candidate.

limitations: Automated AI review performed in a single agent session. It is not organisational independence, not human confirmation, and not a qualified-checker result (master-prompt clause 2.9).
human_approval_status is 'pending' for every record covered by this review, and for this review record itself. No human reviewer signed any of them.
No record covered by this review carries production authority or product verification credit, and this review asserts none.

THIS IS A DIGEST ATTESTATION AND A RE-DERIVATION, NOT A RE-APPROVAL. Every digest in reviewed_ids was computed from the named file's bytes at the time of this pass, so it attests that the digest matches the file as it now stands. It does not attest that any human or any earlier review confirmed the content.
No finding record was modified by this pass. Where a finding record is defective, the defect is recorded here and in the dispositions below; repair is left to the record owner.

corpus.py was NOT modified. The metric and rule observations in this review were read from the tool's source; changing a tool or a metric in order to improve a reported number would be metric gaming and was avoided.

SCOPE LIMIT, STATED RATHER THAN GLOSSED: this review re-derived the asserted CONDITION of each of the 14 records and checked the meta-fields named in its findings. It did NOT independently re-run the unit-test sweep that FB2-REV-FND-000031, -000033, -000034, -000035, -000036, -000037 and -000038 report on: those records' subject matter is CMock, FreeRTOS preprocessor behaviour and Ceedling test outcomes, and re-running them is outside what this pass could do on a host whose load average exceeded 380. For those seven the finding-level claims were checked against the source and the harness configuration where the record cites them by line, and the citation at FB2-REV-FND-000199 is the result of doing so; the pass counts and per-test verdicts inside those records are recorded as asserted by the session that ran them and were NOT independently reproduced here.

FB2-REV-FND-000037 is dispositioned 'deferred' and its record does not state a trigger that would bring it back, which the vocabulary requires of 'deferred'. That is recorded as an observation in results_summary rather than raised as a finding, because a second read of the record found the omission is described in prose inside its resolution ('STILL OPEN, and SHARPER than when this record was raised'), so the information exists for a reader even though it is not in a named field. A reader looking for a machine-readable trigger will not find one.

The two new findings this review raises are defects in the finding family's EVIDENCE and PROVENANCE layers. Neither alleges that a covered record reaches a wrong engineering conclusion: in both cases the record's verdict is correct and survives the defect. That distinction is the reason both are medium and not high.

Finding records 000023 to 000029 are NOT named in this review and were not reviewed here; they are synthetic_reference and are named, with the one targeted check stated in scope, by the sibling record FB2-REV-000023.
review_method: For each record named in reviewed_ids: (a) read the record in full; (b) re-derive its asserted condition from the corpus bytes it cites - the link registries with their documented precedence order, docs/artifacts/tools/corpus.py read as text, and the working-tree C sources it cites by line - rather than reading the condition off the record; (c) assess the severity against what the record actually asserts and what would follow from it being wrong; (d) check the disposition against docs/artifacts/governance/finding-disposition-vocabulary.md and against the schema enum, and require an owner and a named closing action for anything not 'resolved'; (e) verify that a currency proof exists and that it agrees with the corpus, and supply the re-derivation myself where it does not. Coverage was computed by an independent script written from scratch for this pass, not by corpus.py.
